title: O, Here, If Ever, God of Love
description: O, Here, If Ever, God of Love in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emily Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 158, “Communion”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, here, if ev-er, God of love! Let strife and ha-tred cease; And ev-ery thought har-mo-nious move, And ev-ery heart be peace.

lines: O, here, if ever, God of love!
Not here, where met to think of him
Shall mortal passions come to dim
No, gracious Master, not in vain
Thy life of love hath been;
The peace thou gav'st may yet remain,
Though thou no more art seen.
Thy kingdom come! we watch, we wait,
When heaven shall ope its glorious gate,
And God be all in all.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Emily Taylor died in 1872.
credits: Words by Emily Taylor (1795–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
